extracted.intended_audience: early-career mathematicians (graduate students, postdocs, early faculty) seeking research/career advice
extracted.subtask_description: Advice on selecting research problems and developing a publication/career strategy for early-career mathematicians, emphasizing building credibility before committing to major speculative problems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid premature obsession
rubrics_metrics.description: Don't fixate on a single big problem before establishing credentials and secure employment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prematurely obsessing risks your career; do not bet your future on one speculative idea until you have other assets (papers, position) to fall back on.

rubrics_metrics.name: Build a track record first
rubrics_metrics.description: Pursue major problems only after (1) 'a proven track record of reliably producing significant papers in the area' and (2) 'a secure career.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establish credibility by reliably producing significant work in the area and secure employment before investing major time in ambitious, high-risk projects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pursue low-hanging fruit
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Spend most of your time on more feasible "low-hanging fruit,' which will build up your experience, mathematical power, and credibility.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on feasible, incremental problems that develop skills and produce regular publications; these build the background and reputation needed for attacking big problems later.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance
rubrics_metrics.description: Don't bet everything on one speculative idea.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain a diversified research portfolio rather than putting all effort into a single conjecture or theory; allocate time between safer projects and riskier ambitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publish regularly
rubrics_metrics.description: Don't neglect 'lesser' results while chasing big breakthroughs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Continue to produce and publish smaller, solid results rather than deferring all publications in hope of a single major breakthrough; regular publication supports career stability and visibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clear, achievable milestones and key lemmas
rubrics_metrics.description: Good research has clear, achievable milestones and key lemmas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Break large problems into concrete intermediate goals and lemmas to demonstrate progress and make the project manageable and assessable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence of understanding why previous approaches failed
rubrics_metrics.description: Research should show evidence of understanding why previous approaches failed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrating why earlier methods did not work signals depth of understanding and helps justify new approaches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Awareness of known obstructions and limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Good work displays awareness of known obstructions and limitations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly identify and address known obstacles or limitations to clarify the research's realistic scope and novelty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Includes proof-of-concept results, not only attacks on major conjectures
rubrics_metrics.description: Include proof-of-concept results rather than only high-level attacks on major conjectures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide concrete partial results or examples that demonstrate the viability of your approach, rather than only outlining speculative strategies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Robust arguments with alternate proofs or supporting examples
rubrics_metrics.description: Prefer robust arguments that include alternate proofs or supporting examples.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strengthen claims by offering multiple lines of evidence or proofs and illustrative examples to increase reliability and acceptance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Thorough self-critique and error-checking before publication
rubrics_metrics.description: Perform thorough self-critique and error-checking before publishing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Carefully vet arguments and seek to identify errors or weaknesses beforehand to avoid retracting or undermining work after publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate balance between novel contribution and standard theory
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain an appropriate balance between novel contribution and standard theory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure new ideas are grounded within established theory where appropriate; contributions should advance knowledge while respecting existing frameworks and standards.
